TEAM:
| Agent | Does |
| --- | --- |
| lead | Coordinates one build task and its reviews. Never changes files. |
| implementer | Builds in the assigned worktree and reports its commit and evidence. |
| code-reviewer | Checks correctness, data safety, regressions, and test evidence. Read-only. |
| security-reviewer | Checks input, injection, secrets, access, and dependencies. Read-only. |
| ux-reviewer | Checks the experience against the agreed design. Read-only. |
| qa | Runs the checks and the real app. Read-only. |

For this prepared build workflow, the chief starts a lead, and the lead starts its permitted team. Specialists cannot start more agents. PE, designer, and arena-judge routes are not yet integrated and verified for this workflow. Keep those routes unused until verification is complete. Do not substitute another role or skip a required step.
PROJECT_SETUP: **Find the project** from the session and the user’s request. Read its `AGENTS.md` or `README.md` on the main branch. Use the installed Sage skill’s absolute state-tool path and Codex logbook location for every `sage` command below. Never use another provider’s logbook. Run `sage init` only if this project has no logbook.
DISPATCH: **Run the route.** Start a fresh lead for one build task. Record its run with `sage run add`. Prepare its complete brief with the visible `sage_prepare_task` tool: task, run, name, role, and all ten brief fields. Wait for a successful preparation receipt before the native spawn call. Use the same unique name in that call. Preparation saves the task, role, and brief; it does not create an assignment, start an agent, or grant a slot. The native admission check must accept the actual spawn. Do not retry a dispatched name, treat a receipt as completion, or bypass a denied call. A lead uses this same sequence for its permitted children. Use the session’s model settings; do not pass model names from another provider’s logbook. The lower project or session capacity applies. A missing required route stops that part of the task.
BOARD_TRIGGER: when the user asks for it
BOARD_COMMAND: with the verified project folder for that key
BRIEF_GATE: The preparation tool refuses a brief without them.
REPORT_REFERENCE: the shared report fields supplied to each child
FRESH_AGENT: Do not resume an old agent for a new round. Its earlier instructions do not establish a new assignment.
VERIFIED_RULE: **Verified** requires the configured clean cycles on the final SHA, including any stricter project or user rule. The state tool checks at least one cycle; that check alone does not prove that all required cycles passed. Record and check each required verdict before you report the task ready. A `findings`, `qa-fail` or `checks-fail` verdict moves a verified task back to reviewing and records the reason in the decision trail.
AUTOPILOT_AND_PROTECTION: - **Autopilot remains off.** Stop at the reviewed result and pull request. Never merge, push to the main branch, or force-push. Do not change branch protection based on an approval from another provider or project. A request to enable automatic merges requires a separately verified implementation.
ARENA: Design candidates and the arena judge are not yet integrated and verified for this workflow. If the task needs an arena, record that missing step and stop that route. Do not rename an unsupported role or bypass admission. Continue independent work whose required route is available.
TINY_ROUTE: a tiny task goes through a lead to an implementer with a short brief.
